svg.title: The first synchronization
svg.desc: With the connection saved and synchronization still off, a dry-run lists what the first run would write, and Getting started estimates how long the first synchronization takes. Then scheduled synchronization is turned on and saved. Nextcloud's cron starts the background job of the app every five minutes at most, and once the interval has passed, a run exports the documents that Paperless added last first, up to the batch size, 100 by default; its report counts the others as skipped. While documents are left, the next run takes the next batch after the interval: with the defaults, 5,000 documents take 50 runs, four hours or more. Then the archive is complete, and each later run changes only what changed in Paperless. Instead, a large archive can be imported in one go on the server, with the schedule still off, by occ paperless_sync:run --unlimited. Your steps are orange, the questions indigo, the runs blue and the complete archive green.
